source.quote: * **api:** add support for new API version 2026-10-21

tasks.reasoning:
The repo pins @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.71.2, which keeps sending API version 2023-06-01, so nothing breaks today. When the repo upgrades to 1.0.0, it must make these edits together: remove temperature (and any top_p/top_k) from aiHandler.js:233, fix message construction for the MessageParam union type, verify no document or citation placement errors, and decide on OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation. No Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry SDKs are in use. This is an optional upgrade with no forced date.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- anthropic:2026-10-21-api-version-2026-10-21 (api-version): New Claude API version 2026-10-21 (anthropic-version header); SDKs older than the new majors keep sending 2023-06-01. SDK 1.0.0 sends anthropic-version 2026-10-21 by default. The repo's 0.71.2 keeps sending 2023-06-01, so the API version moves only with this SDK bump.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "This guide lists the code changes for moving from API version `2023-06-01` to `2026-10-21`."
- anthropic:2026-10-21-sampling-params-removed (field-removed): In API version 2026-10-21, temperature, top_p and top_k in Messages and Batch requests return 400. aiHandler.js:233 sends temperature. That returns 400 only under API version 2026-10-21, and SDK 1.0.0 also removes the parameter from its types. Dropping temperature is part of this upgrade's edit.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "In `2026-10-21`, a request that sends `temperature`, `top_p`, or `top_k` returns a 400 error, even at the parameter’s default value."
- anthropic:2026-10-21-document-citations-user-assistant-errors (other): In API version 2026-10-21, document blocks in assistant messages and citations on text blocks in user messages return 400. Applies only under API version 2026-10-21, which arrives with this bump. The agent should check that the messages built in aiHandler.js put no document blocks in assistant turns and no citations on text blocks in user turns.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "In `2026-10-21`, a request that places a `document` block directly in an `assistant` message returns a 400 error."
- anthropic:2026-10-14-ts-sdk-otel-default (other): TypeScript SDK 0.134.0 auto-creates OpenTelemetry spans and trace headers if a global tracer provider exists (unsure if affects; opt out with openTelemetry:false). The jump from 0.71.2 to 1.0.0 passes 0.134.0. The agent should check whether the app registers a global OpenTelemetry tracer provider, and set openTelemetry:false if new spans are unwanted.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "If your app registers a global tracer provider, the SDK will create spans with it after upgrading, and they'll be exported with the rest of your traces."

callSites.why: messages.create sends temperature, which SDK 1.0.0 removes and API 2026-10-21 rejects with 400. The MessageParam union type change may affect how the messages and content array is built.

## npm @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.0.0 sends API version 2026-10-21 by default; MessageParam becomes a union, temperature/top_p/top_k removed, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry SDKs must move to v1 too [Needs review]

### Change

Bumped @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.71.2 -> ^1.0.0 via npm. In aiHandler.js, removed temperature from the Anthropic messages.create call (the OpenAI path keeps it) and changed response.content[0].text to join all text blocks. Added test/anthropic-sdk1.test.js, registered as check anthropic-sdk1. It drives generateResponse through the real 1.0.0 client with a stubbed fetch. It asserts the anthropic-version header is 2026-10-21, no temperature/top_p/top_k in the body, and that the text is returned.

Files touched:
- `aiHandler.js`
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `test/anthropic-sdk1.test.js`

### Why

API version 2026-10-21 (the SDK 1.0.0 default) returns 400 when temperature, top_p or top_k are sent. aiHandler.js:233 sent temperature.

> * **api:** add support for new API version 2026-10-21

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| anthropic-sdk1 | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- anthropic-sdk1, added by the agent: `node test/anthropic-sdk1.test.js` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Real API behaviour at 2026-10-21 was not tested.
- Pinned model ids claude-opus-4-20250514 and claude-sonnet-4-20250514 may be retiring; not checked.
- The repo has no other test or type-check scripts; baseline checks were only the added one.
- The license of the SDK changes from MIT to Apache-2.0.
- package-lock.json churn was not reviewed.
- The agent wrote no test of this change and gave no reason why none can be written.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- Claude calls no longer receive the per-model temperature (0.3/0.5), so output sampling uses API defaults. The UI and MODELS config still carry the temperature, which is now used only for OpenAI.
- Response text now concatenates all text blocks instead of reading only the first block.
- The SDK now sends anthropic-version 2026-10-21 by default.
- Document/citation placement: messages are plain-string user/assistant turns, with no document or citation blocks, so there is no 400 risk.
- OpenTelemetry: no tracer provider is registered in the repo, so openTelemetry:false was not set.
- No Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry SDKs are in use, and there are no raw-HTTP Anthropic calls.

preparation.reasoning: Plain Node/Express app with no codegen, build, or install-hook steps. The only scripts are start and a placeholder test. No checks were detected, so nothing needs preparing.

review.summary: The diff covers the one Anthropic call site (aiHandler.js:233). It drops `temperature` as the 2026-10-21 API requires and makes text extraction tolerate non-text blocks. The new test confirms the `anthropic-version` header and that no sampling params are sent, but only against a stubbed module and a fake fetch. It does not prove that the real v1 CommonJS export works with `new Anthropic(...)`, that the hard-coded model IDs are still accepted, or that anything works on a live call. Dropping temperature also changes how all Claude answers are generated. needs-review is the right grade.

concerns.issue: The test replaces `require('@anthropic-ai/sdk')` with its own `Stubbed` class through `Module._load`, so aiHandler.js never sees the real v1 module's export shape. aiHandler.js line 2 does `const Anthropic = require('@anthropic-ai/sdk')` and then `new Anthropic(...)`. If v1's CommonJS entry no longer exports the constructor as `module.exports` and exposes only `.default` or `.Anthropic`, production would throw at `initAI` while this test still passes. The test's own `Real.default || Real` hedge hints that the shape is uncertain. I could not confirm v1's CJS export from memory; check `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/sdk/index.js` in v1.

The model IDs `claude-opus-4-20250514` and `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` (around line 234) are unchanged. I could not confirm they are still served under API version 2026-10-21, and the stubbed test cannot show it. The 'claude-opus-4.5' label mapping to an Opus 4 ID was already there before this PR, but it is worth checking while the call is being revisited.

Removing `temperature` means every Claude call now runs at the server default. Before, these were 0.3 from MODELS, or the per-call value in synthesis (answerWithDecomposition) and the CoT path. The API change forces this, but answers become less deterministic. `MODELS[*].temperature` for the Claude entries and `options.temperature` are now silently ignored for Anthropic. A comment, or removing those config values, would make that clear.

The return value changed from `response.content[0].text` to joining all text blocks. That is generally better: it no longer returns undefined when the first block is not text. It is still a behaviour change: multiple text blocks are now concatenated with no separator, and a response with no text blocks returns '' instead of undefined.

The new test is not wired into `npm test`, which is still `echo ... && exit 1`, so it will not run in CI unless the check runner calls it directly. The lockfile also shows the SDK license changing from MIT to Apache-2.0, plus new transitive dependencies (@opentelemetry/api, standardwebhooks). Both are worth a quick compliance and size check.

Only the 'claude-sonnet-4' path with multi-query and decomposition disabled is exercised. The Opus mapping, the system-prompt path with chat history (MessageParam is now a union per the change notes), and the decomposition and synthesis paths are not covered. The OpenAI path is not covered either; it is unchanged.

checkFirst: In a plain Node REPL with v1 installed, run `const A = require('@anthropic-ai/sdk'); new A({apiKey:'x'})` and confirm it constructs without the test's Module._load stub.
Confirm in the v1 SDK types or the Anthropic models docs that claude-sonnet-4-20250514 and claude-opus-4-20250514 are valid under API version 2026-10-21, and make one live call.
Check with the product owner that losing temperature 0.3 on Claude answers is acceptable for citation-heavy output.
